title: Protocol and Machine Anew
premise: Hazel Halloran smuggles memories between the silent worlds of the Meridian system, carrying grief, testimony, and contraband through a customs web that watches everything. When gravity fails for nine seconds, Hazel's hidden cargo — a memory chip containing proof of a massacre on the station Vesper's Rest — activates, revealing that the ruling Concordat erased the event from every archive. Hunted by Concordat enforcers and betrayed by the broker who sold them the chip, Hazel and their makeshift crew must smuggle the truth to the last independent relay before the Concordat's memory-scrubbing fleet reaches it. They succeed at terrible cost, and the system's worlds, given back their shared past, begin speaking to each other again.
about_author: O. M. Joubert is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade aboard cargo vessels before turning to fiction. They write about people who carry things — cargo, secrets, other people's memories — across distances that were never meant to be crossed.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Hazel runs a memory-smuggling route between two worlds that severed diplomatic ties years ago, introducing their patched-together ship and found-family crew: engineer Sefu, pilot Wren, and stowaway archivist Ilsa. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: weary tenderness — this fragile crew is the only home Hazel has left.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Gravity fails across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; ships drift, people float, and something ancient passes through the relay network. Hazel's hidden cargo chip wakes and broadcasts a fragment: screams from Vesper's Rest. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: dread — the universe just noticed them.

chapters.title: What the Chip Remembers
chapters.summary: Ilsa decodes the chip: a first-person memory of a Concordat massacre on Vesper's Rest, twelve thousand dead, scrubbed from every archive. Hazel realizes the broker who sold it knew what it was. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: horrified resolve — someone has to carry this truth.

chapters.title: Customs and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Concordat enforcers board the ship at Meridian Gate, hunting the 'anomalous data event.' Hazel's forged manifests hold, but an inspector recognizes the chip's signature and lets them go — with a warning that suggests he remembers Vesper's Rest too. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into solidarity.

chapters.title: The Broker's Debt
chapters.summary: Hazel confronts broker Ansel Vey on the pleasure moon Calloway, learning he sold the chip to draw Concordat attention away from a second copy. Vey offers Hazel a cut to run his errand; Hazel refuses, then discovers Vey sold them out anyway. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: betrayal — even smugglers' honor has a price.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Pursued, the crew fractures: Sefu wants to dump the chip and survive; Wren's sister died on Vesper's Rest and she needs the truth; Ilsa argues archives are how the dead stay alive. A near-catastrophic docking accident forces them to trust each other with their lives. POV: Sefu. Emotional beat: found family forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Vesper's Rest
chapters.summary: The crew reaches the quarantined, officially 'empty' station and finds survivors living off-grid in the dark, erased from every census. Their testimony matches the chip. The Concordat arrives to finish the erasure. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief made concrete — and the dead refusing to stay dead.

chapters.title: The Scrubbing Fleet
chapters.summary: A running battle through the station's gravity-torn wreckage as the crew escapes with survivor witnesses and the second chip. Sefu stays behind to hold the docking clamps and is captured. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: sacrifice — the family pays its first blood price.

chapters.title: The Last Relay
chapters.summary: Climax: Hazel and Wren race the scrubbing fleet to the independent relay at the system's edge, using the nine-second gravity anomaly as a slingshot only smugglers would dare. They broadcast the massacre to every world at once as the Concordat closes in. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: defiant hope against impossible odds.

chapters.title: Protocol, Anew
chapters.summary: The truth spreads; worlds that stopped speaking reopen channels, and the Concordat's legitimacy cracks. Hazel, wounded and stripped of their smuggling license, negotiates Sefu's release — the enforcer from Chapter 4 testifies. The crew, no longer outlaws of necessity, chooses to stay together. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: belonging — a family that chose itself, and a system learning to remember.
